page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, this instance is equipped with a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. It includes 84.0 GB of system memory, translating to an exceptionally high allocation of 42.0 GB per physical core. Additionally, the server comes bundled with 236 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its Geekbench single-core score of 2342.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates. However, due to its low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with a poor stress-ng multi-core rating and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2884.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are also relatively low, with large-block read and write speeds categorized as poor, though the overall PassMark memory score remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4-2mds_v2 offers a highly specialized resource density, prioritizing massive memory capacity per core over parallel compute power. This makes it a qualitative fit for workloads that are heavily constrained by memory footprint rather than multi-threaded CPU scaling. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive single-threaded applications, small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight text processing tasks that benefit from high single-core clock speeds and a large memory buffer.
